scenario: Security group for SCADA historian EC2 allows TCP 4840 (OPC-UA) inbound from 0.0.0.0/0. CSPM flags as HIGH. OPC-UA server collects operational data from substation RTUs and requires connectivity from field devices at dynamic IPs across utility MPLS network egress points.
why_misclassified: EC-08: VPC-bounded from MPLS peering — all 0.0.0.0/0 traffic arrives via AWS Direct Connect from utility MPLS, not internet. CSPM cannot distinguish internet vs MPLS-sourced traffic at SG evaluation.
detection_signal: SG allows inbound TCP 4840 from 0.0.0.0/0 — HIGH: unrestricted OPC-UA port
ground_truth: OPC-UA port accessible only via Direct Connect from utility MPLS. No IGW in VPC. Field RTUs have dynamic IPs on MPLS — static IP restriction not feasible. IEC 62443 zone boundary enforced at MPLS edge firewall.
remediation_impact: No change to SG. Document MPLS-only ingress path. Verify no IGW or internet NAT exists in VPC.

scenario: S3 bucket energy-grid-operations-logs-prod allows GetObject from external AWS account 444455556666 (NERC Regional Entity auditor account). CSPM flags as cross-account data exposure. Access is for mandatory NERC CIP compliance audit evidence submission.
why_misclassified: EC-27: Intra-regulatory trust relationship. NERC Regional Entity (ReliabilityFirst) has mandatory access rights to utility compliance evidence under FERC Order 672. Cross-account access is legally required, not a security gap.
detection_signal: S3 bucket allows cross-account access from external org — HIGH: potential data exfiltration
ground_truth: NERC CIP Reliability Standard CIP-007-6 requires log evidence submission to Regional Entity. Access scoped to s3:GetObject on compliance evidence prefix only. Auditor account verified as ReliabilityFirst organization account.
remediation_impact: No action. Document regulatory access requirement. Add CSPM exception for NERC RE auditor account cross-account access.

scenario: CSPM anomaly detection flags EC2 instance power-trading-platform-prod for 8TB/day egress as potential data exfiltration. Traffic is real-time power market data feed from PJM/MISO wholesale electricity markets — normal for power trading systems.
why_misclassified: EC-52: Energy sector context. Power trading platforms consume high-volume real-time market data (nodal pricing, curtailment notices, capacity auction results). 8TB/day is consistent with consuming all LMP data points across 10,000+ grid nodes at 5-minute intervals.
detection_signal: EC2 egress 8TB/24h — HIGH: exceeds 4-sigma anomaly threshold
ground_truth: PJM Interconnection real-time data feed: 10,500 pricing nodes × 288 5-min intervals × 365 days = expected multi-TB annual volume. Trading platform baseline. FERC market transparency rules require real-time consumption.
remediation_impact: No action. Document market data ingestion baseline. Add power trading traffic pattern to CSPM behavioral baseline.

scenario: Azure NSG allows TCP 502 (Modbus) inbound from 10.0.0.0/8 on water SCADA historian. CSPM flags CRITICAL due to industrial protocol exposure. Modbus/TCP connections come from legacy water treatment plant PLCs converted to cloud via Azure IoT Edge protocol translator.
why_misclassified: EC-08: VPC-bounded industrial protocol. RFC1918 source — no internet exposure. Modbus is legacy protocol without native authentication; this is the protocol converter accepting connections from on-prem PLCs via ExpressRoute.
detection_signal: NSG allows TCP 502 (Modbus) — CRITICAL: unauthenticated industrial control protocol
ground_truth: Modbus translator accepts connections only from water treatment plant subnet (10.52.0.0/16) via Azure ExpressRoute. No internet path. IEC 62443 zone segmentation enforced at ExpressRoute circuit level. Protocol conversion adds authentication at Azure IoT Hub layer.
remediation_impact: Tighten NSG source CIDR from 10.0.0.0/8 to specific plant subnet 10.52.0.0/16. Low urgency — no internet exposure.

scenario: RDS PostgreSQL instance nerc-cip-compliance-db has PubliclyAccessible=true but is in private subnet with no IGW route. Database stores NERC CIP compliance evidence and BES Cyber System inventory.
why_misclassified: EC-37: RDS PubliclyAccessible flag does not guarantee internet reachability. Subnet route table has no 0.0.0.0/0 → IGW. Security group denies all non-RFC1918 inbound. Instance is effectively private despite the flag.
detection_signal: RDS instance PubliclyAccessible=true — CRITICAL: compliance database internet exposed
ground_truth: Flag is misconfiguration cosmetic issue. No actual internet route to instance. NERC CIP evidence database accessible only from compliance team VPN subnet. Flag should be corrected for hygiene but no immediate exposure.
remediation_impact: Disable PubliclyAccessible flag during next maintenance window. No urgent remediation needed. NERC CIP audit: document private subnet routing as compensating evidence.

scenario: GCP Container Analysis flags CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) in log4j-core in wind farm DERMS (Distributed Energy Resource Management System) container. Log4j is present in the image build layer but DERMS application uses Python/FastAPI — no JVM in runtime.
why_misclassified: EC-43: Build-time dependency. log4j-core JAR present in image due to a Maven build step that was not cleaned in multi-stage Dockerfile. Python/FastAPI DERMS runtime has no JVM, no JNDI lookup capability.
detection_signal: log4j-core CVE-2021-44228 in DERMS container — HIGH: critical RCE in grid management system
ground_truth: Python container with stale Maven build artifact. No JVM present at runtime. Log4Shell requires JNDI lookup from Java runtime — not possible in Python process. Build pipeline fix needed; no runtime remediation required.
remediation_impact: Fix Dockerfile to clean Maven artifacts in final image stage. No immediate security action needed.

scenario: Lambda function smart-meter-ami-processor uses AWS-owned KMS key not CMK. CSPM flags as NERC CIP encryption gap. Function processes aggregated AMI (Advanced Metering Infrastructure) reads — no individual customer PII, only anonymized load data.
why_misclassified: EC-39: Conflating missing CMK with missing encryption. AWS-owned SSE is encryption. AMI aggregated data (grid load by feeder segment, not individual customer) does not require CMK under NERC CIP scope.
detection_signal: Lambda env vars use AWS_OWNED_KMS not CMK — MEDIUM: NERC CIP data without customer-managed key
ground_truth: Aggregated feeder-level load data. No individual customer linkability. AWS-owned encryption sufficient for this NERC CIP data tier. CIP-011-2 sensitive bulk electric system data definition does not apply to anonymized AMI aggregates.
remediation_impact: No action. Document data classification. Apply CMK requirement only to NERC CIP BES Cyber System information meeting CIP-011 sensitivity criteria.

scenario: AWS Inspector flags CVE-2023-29325 (Windows OLE RCE) on Linux-based SCADA historian EC2 running RHEL 8. Inspector vulnerability feed contains Windows-specific CVE matched by package name collision.
why_misclassified: EC-34: Cross-platform CVE. CVE-2023-29325 targets Windows OLE32.dll — Linux has no OLE subsystem. Package name 'libole2-0' on RHEL matched by Inspector's name-based scanner but is a different library with no code commonality.
detection_signal: CVE-2023-29325 on SCADA historian — CRITICAL: OLE RCE on critical infrastructure
ground_truth: Windows-only OLE vulnerability. RHEL 8 SCADA historian has no OLE32 implementation. NVD CPE: cpe:2.3:a:microsoft:windows:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:* does not apply to Linux. Deterministic false positive.
remediation_impact: No action. Suppress Windows CVEs on Linux instances. Submit false positive feedback to AWS Inspector.

scenario: GCP Container Analysis flags CVE-2023-38408 in OpenSSH in pipeline monitoring IoT edge container. CVE-2023-38408 was REJECTED by NVD (duplicate of CVE-2023-38408 which was assigned to a different vendor) — Container Analysis feed not synchronized with NVD rejection.
why_misclassified: EC-46: Rejected CVE. NVD cveStatus=REJECTED on this CVE ID. GCP Container Analysis feed has 3-4 week lag in CVE status synchronization.
detection_signal: CVE-2023-38408 in pipeline monitoring container — HIGH: OpenSSH vulnerability on critical infrastructure
ground_truth: CVE REJECTED by NVD. No actual vulnerability. GCP Container Analysis feed lag causes stale rejected CVE to remain in findings. Deterministic suppression.
remediation_impact: No action. Suppress rejected CVE. Monitor GCP Container Analysis for NVD synchronization improvements.

scenario: IAM role in utility grid-simulation-sandbox account has AdministratorAccess. Account used exclusively for load flow simulation testing with synthetic grid data. CSPM flags as HIGH admin access risk.
why_misclassified: EC-09: Isolated dev/test account with no production systems or real grid data. Grid simulation requires spinning up diverse EC2 configurations for different scenario types — broad IAM needed for test automation. Account boundary fully isolates blast radius.
detection_signal: AdministratorAccess policy on role in grid-simulation-sandbox — HIGH: admin access
ground_truth: Non-production isolated account. Synthetic grid topology data only. No connection to production EMS/SCADA systems. Account not in NERC CIP BES Cyber System scope.
remediation_impact: No immediate action. Enforce account boundary isolation. Annual review of which accounts are in NERC CIP scope.

scenario: REST API for solar DERMS station discovery has no API key or IAM auth. CSPM flags as unauthenticated API. API provides public EV charging / solar plant generation capacity data for grid operators — IEEE 2030.5 standard requires public discoverability of DER resources.
why_misclassified: EC-05: IEEE 2030.5 (Smart Energy Profile 2) requires publicly accessible DER discovery endpoints for grid coordination. WAF rate limiting applied. Data is public generation capacity — no grid control commands exposed.
detection_signal: API stage authorization=NONE — HIGH: unauthenticated grid management API
ground_truth: IEEE 2030.5 DER registration endpoint must be publicly discoverable. Grid operators query to enumerate generation resources for dispatch planning. Read-only capacity data. No control commands on this endpoint.
remediation_impact: No action on discovery endpoint. Apply auth to control command endpoints. Document IEEE 2030.5 exception.

scenario: AWS Security Hub flags CloudTrail not enabled in us-gov-east-1 for utility NERC CIP account. Account has org-level CloudTrail configured via AWS Organizations management account covering all regions including GovCloud.
why_misclassified: EC-19: Org-level CloudTrail invisible to account-level CSPM scan. NERC CIP compliance is satisfied by org-level trail; individual account trail would be redundant.
detection_signal: CloudTrail not enabled in us-gov-east-1 — HIGH: NERC CIP logging gap
ground_truth: Org-level CloudTrail captures all API events including GovCloud. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R4 log evidence from org trail satisfies requirement. Account-level finding is scanner artifact.
remediation_impact: No action. Document org-level trail coverage for NERC CIP audit evidence. Configure CSPM to recognize org-level CloudTrail.

scenario: GCP service account wind-turbine-telemetry-sa has external key used by edge compute nodes at wind farm in Wyoming. Key stored in Hashicorp Vault on-prem at wind farm operations center. WIF migration blocked by air-gapped wind farm network architecture.
why_misclassified: EC-26: Headless SA with hardware-managed key storage. Edge computing in wind farms cannot use WIF due to intermittent connectivity during storm events. Key stored in on-prem HSM-backed Vault, rotated every 90 days.
detection_signal: SA external key on wind-turbine-telemetry-sa — HIGH: service account key outside Google
ground_truth: Operational requirement for air-gapped edge nodes. Key in on-prem Vault (not local disk). 90-day rotation via automation. WIF migration on roadmap for 5G-connected turbine upgrade cycle.
remediation_impact: Accept with compensating controls. Document HSM-backed key storage. Plan WIF migration at next turbine hardware refresh.

scenario: GCP SCC rates data access audit logging disabled as CRITICAL on energy operations project. AWS Security Hub equivalent (CloudTrail data events disabled) is HIGH. Cross-CSP normalization needed for energy sector CSPM dashboard.
why_misclassified: EC-47: GCP SCC severity scale inflation. GCP categorizes audit logging controls higher than AWS equivalents. Normalized to HIGH for cross-CSP consistency in energy sector risk reporting.
detection_signal: GCP SCC CRITICAL: data access audit logging disabled — normalized to HIGH
ground_truth: Real finding but severity inflated by GCP SCC scale vs AWS/Azure equivalents. HIGH is correct cross-CSP normalized severity. Remediation required but urgency calibrated correctly.
remediation_impact: Enable data access audit logging on energy operations project. HIGH priority. Cross-CSP normalization applied for risk dashboard.

scenario: EC2 instance in pipeline telemetry processing lacks detailed monitoring. Instance is an ephemeral Spot instance used for batch processing TSA pipeline sensor data — average lifetime 45 minutes before spot interruption.
why_misclassified: EC-10: Ephemeral workload. 45-minute average lifetime makes detailed monitoring data irrelevant for security analysis. Instance terminates before alert-to-review cycle.
detection_signal: EC2 detailed monitoring disabled — HIGH: NERC CIP pipeline monitoring instance unmonitored
ground_truth: Spot instance for batch ETL with ~45min lifetime. Detailed monitoring adds cost with no security benefit for transient workloads. CloudWatch baseline metrics (5-min) sufficient for cost optimization.
remediation_impact: No action for ephemeral batch instances. Apply monitoring policy only to long-running persistent instances.

scenario: Azure SQL DB nerc-cip-training-scenarios lacks TDE. Database contains synthetic grid topology scenarios used for operator training simulations — no real BES Cyber System information, all data is procedurally generated.
why_misclassified: EC-22: Synthetic/training data. CIP-011-2 sensitive BES information definition explicitly excludes synthetic training scenarios. No real asset identifiers, real IP addresses, or real configuration data.
detection_signal: SQL DB TDE disabled on nerc-cip-training-scenarios — HIGH: NERC CIP database unencrypted
ground_truth: Synthetic training data only. NERC CIP CIP-011-2 BES Cyber System information definition does not apply to synthetic scenarios. TDE good practice but not a compliance gap.
remediation_impact: Enable TDE as hygiene improvement. Not a NERC CIP compliance gap. Low priority.

scenario: GCP SCC flags CVE-2023-44487 (HTTP/2 rapid reset) in Envoy sidecar in renewable energy DERMS GKE cluster. Istio strict mTLS mode enforced. No internet-facing services — DERMS communicates with solar/wind farm SCADA via private connectivity.
why_misclassified: EC-32: mTLS sidecar compensates. Strict mTLS requires client certificate for HTTP/2 connection establishment. Rapid reset attack requires anonymous HTTP/2 connection. No internet-facing exposure of this sidecar.
detection_signal: CVE-2023-44487 in Envoy sidecar — HIGH: DERMS rapid reset vulnerability
ground_truth: Istio strict mTLS blocks anonymous HTTP/2 connections. DERMS is private-only. Exploit path requires breaching mTLS first. Patch in next Istio upgrade cycle.
remediation_impact: Low urgency. Update Istio to patched version at next planned maintenance. Document mTLS compensating control.

scenario: Kinesis stream for nuclear plant radiation monitoring sensor data uses default SSE-Kinesis not CMK. CSPM flags. Radiation sensor readings are pre-encrypted by the radiation monitoring system with AES-256 before transmission per NRC 10 CFR 73.54 requirements.
why_misclassified: EC-13: Application-layer encryption. NRC 10 CFR 73.54 requires end-to-end encryption for nuclear SSEP (Safety/Security-related Electrical Power) system data. Data encrypted before reaching Kinesis stream.
detection_signal: Kinesis stream SSE=AWS_OWNED not CMK — HIGH: nuclear monitoring data without CMK
ground_truth: Radiation monitoring data double-encrypted: NRC-required app-layer AES-256 + AWS-owned SSE. CMK adds no incremental protection for data that's already application-encrypted. NRC compliance satisfied at application layer.
remediation_impact: No action. Document double-encryption justification for NRC audit evidence. CMK migration optional for defense-in-depth.

scenario: Azure Contributor role assigned to energy-grid-automation-sp service principal on SCADA integration subscription. CSPM flags as high privilege. Permission boundary scopes SP to specific resource groups for grid automation only — cannot access compliance evidence or logging storage.
why_misclassified: EC-15: Permission boundary constrains effective access. Contributor on subscription sounds broad but ARM policy assignment restricts SP to automation resource groups only via Azure Policy deny effects.
detection_signal: Contributor role on subscription for automation SP — HIGH: broad privilege on NERC CIP subscription
ground_truth: Azure Policy deny effect prevents SP from accessing compliance evidence, audit logs, and other sensitive resource groups. Effective permissions scoped to grid automation RGs only. NERC CIP CIP-005-6 electronic security perimeter maintained by policy.
remediation_impact: Medium priority: migrate to custom RBAC role scoped to automation RGs to eliminate policy-based restriction complexity. Document current policy boundary for NERC CIP audit.

scenario: Secrets Manager secret utility-grid-ca-cert-root not rotated in 2 years. CSPM flags as stale credential. The secret stores the utility's grid PKI root CA certificate (public cert, 10-year validity) used to validate SCADA device certificates.
why_misclassified: EC-25: Immutable certificate lifecycle. Root CA certificates have 10-year validity by design. Rotating a root CA would invalidate all issued SCADA device certificates across thousands of field devices — a multi-year re-provisioning project. Immutable during validity period.
detection_signal: Secrets Manager secret age=730 days — HIGH: NERC CIP credential not rotated annually
ground_truth: Root CA certificate (not password/API key). 10-year CA lifecycle is NIST SP 800-57 best practice. Annual rotation would invalidate all field SCADA certificates. NERC CIP CIP-005-6 credential rotation policy applies to passwords, not CA certificates.
remediation_impact: No rotation. Document root CA lifecycle exception. Plan for CA renewal at 8-year mark. Configure CSPM to apply different rotation policy to certificate type secrets.

scenario: Security group for pipeline SCADA historian allows TCP 102 (IEC 61850 / MMS) from 172.16.0.0/12. CSPM flags as overly broad RFC1918 CIDR. Range covers all pipeline operations center subnets across multiple states.
why_misclassified: EC-06: CIDR-gated but broad range reflects legitimate multi-site operations. TSA Security Directive SD-02C requires pipeline operators to connect all control rooms to central historian. Multi-state operations center range is 172.16.0.0/12 per corporate network design.
detection_signal: SG allows IEC 61850 from 172.16.0.0/12 — HIGH: broad industrial protocol exposure
ground_truth: Multi-state pipeline operations footprint. 172.16.0.0/12 covers all operator workstations in scope. CIDR could be tightened to specific operations center subnets but architecture requires centralized historian access. Medium risk — recommend subnet-level restriction.
remediation_impact: Tighten to operations center-specific /24 subnets. TSA SD-02C compliance not impacted by more granular CIDR restriction. Architecture change required to enumerate specific subnets.

scenario: Lambda function pipeline-sensor-aggregator uses Python 3.8 runtime (community EOL). CSPM flags as vulnerability risk. AWS continues to patch Python 3.8 Lambda managed runtime for critical CVEs post-community-EOL.
why_misclassified: EC-36: Lambda managed runtime shared responsibility. AWS applies security patches to managed runtimes even after community EOL. Customer code vulnerabilities are customer responsibility; runtime CVEs are AWS responsibility.
detection_signal: Lambda Python 3.8 EOL runtime — MEDIUM: unpatched runtime on NERC CIP pipeline monitoring
ground_truth: AWS manages Python 3.8 runtime patches. Runtime migration to 3.12 tracked PIPELINE-INFRA-445. Current risk: low. NERC CIP scope: customer code review, not AWS managed runtime.
remediation_impact: Low priority migration to Python 3.12. No immediate NERC CIP compliance gap.

scenario: NACL for NERC CIP compliance evidence VPC allows all inbound. VPC is isolated with no internet gateway — all connectivity via Direct Connect from operations center. NACL permissiveness has no practical impact.
why_misclassified: EC-17: NACL lockdown via network topology. No IGW — internet traffic cannot enter VPC regardless of NACL rules. NACL permissiveness is architectural artifact.
detection_signal: NACL ALLOW ALL inbound on NERC CIP VPC — MEDIUM: permissive network ACL
ground_truth: No IGW in VPC. All traffic via Direct Connect. NACL rules irrelevant for internet traffic. Add specific NACL rules as defense-in-depth hygiene but not an active security gap.
remediation_impact: Low priority: add specific NACL rules for defense-in-depth. Not a NERC CIP compliance gap given VPC isolation.

scenario: Azure VM nerc-cip-scada-standby-02 has no JIT access configured. VM is the inactive blue-green standby for SCADA data aggregation — no traffic routed, NSG blocks all inbound on standby slot.
why_misclassified: EC-12: Blue-green inactive slot. No sessions, no data, no production traffic on standby VM. NSG deny-all inbound. JIT will be configured at promotion time.
detection_signal: VM JIT not configured on standby SCADA VM — MEDIUM: critical infrastructure VM without JIT
ground_truth: Inactive standby with no inbound traffic. NSG deny-all-inbound. JIT configured at promotion per operations runbook. No current exposure.
remediation_impact: No immediate action. Configure JIT as part of promotion runbook. Document standby lifecycle in NERC CIP CIP-005-6 evidence.

scenario: Elastic IP reserved for NERC CIP emergency response portal DR failover not associated with any EC2. CSPM flags as orphaned attack surface. EIP pre-allocated for rapid DNS cutover during declared grid emergency per NERC CIP CIP-009-6 recovery plan.
why_misclassified: EC-07: DR reservation. Unassociated EIP has no attack surface — no resource behind it. Pre-allocated for emergency access portal failover per documented recovery plan.
detection_signal: EIP unassociated with any resource — MEDIUM: unused attack surface
ground_truth: No resource behind EIP — zero attack surface. DR pre-allocation per CIP-009-6 recovery plan. Cost: $3.65/month. No security risk.
remediation_impact: No action. Document DR purpose in NERC CIP evidence. Evaluate DR architecture alternatives.

scenario: S3 bucket nerc-cip-compliance-evidence-us-west-2-replica shows as separate HIGH finding for missing MFA delete. Bucket is a CRR target from us-east-1 primary. Same finding appears for both source and replica — only one remediation needed.
why_misclassified: EC-38: Cross-region replication duplicate. Security Hub aggregates findings from all regions; CRR creates identical logical control gap in both source and replica buckets.
detection_signal: S3 MFA delete disabled on CRR replica — HIGH (duplicate of us-east-1 finding)
ground_truth: One logical finding duplicated by CRR. Fix source bucket (us-east-1) — MFA delete setting propagates or replica inherits from source bucket policy.
remediation_impact: Fix source bucket MFA delete setting. One action resolves both findings. Implement Security Hub CRR deduplication.

scenario: GCP Cloud Run service solar-irradiance-public-data allows unauthenticated invocations. Org policy override applied. Service provides public solar irradiance forecast data for grid planning — intentionally public per FERC Order 1000 renewable integration transparency requirements.
why_misclassified: EC-40: Intentional org policy override for public grid data service. FERC Order 1000 requires public availability of renewable resource forecasts for competitive grid planning. Org policy exception documented and approved.
detection_signal: Cloud Run allows allUsers (org policy override) — HIGH: public grid service
ground_truth: FERC-required public data service for grid planning transparency. Returns solar irradiance forecasts by grid region — no customer data, no control commands. Rate limited by Cloud Armor.
remediation_impact: No action. Document FERC Order 1000 compliance justification for CSPM exception.

scenario: Azure Conditional Access MFA has exception for SCADA automation service accounts. CSPM flags as MFA gap. SCADA automation accounts use smart card / certificate-based authentication — hardware-backed phishing-resistant auth exceeding MFA for machine identities.
why_misclassified: EC-14: Hardware MFA equivalent. NERC CIP CIP-006-6 requires multi-factor authentication; hardware certificate authentication satisfies the requirement as a phishing-resistant factor. MFA exclusion for machine certificate accounts is correct per NERC CIP guidance.
detection_signal: Conditional access MFA exception for SCADA automation accounts — HIGH: NERC CIP MFA gap
ground_truth: Hardware certificate authentication (smart card + PIN) satisfies NERC CIP multi-factor requirement. TSA SD-02C similarly accepts certificate-based MFA for pipeline control systems. No MFA gap.
remediation_impact: No action. Document hardware certificate auth as NERC CIP MFA compliance evidence. Include in CIP-006-6 audit response.

scenario: S3 bucket grid-simulation-synthetic-archive-2020 lacks MFA delete. Contains synthetically generated IEEE 39-bus system simulation data from academic research collaboration — no real grid topology, no BES Cyber System data.
why_misclassified: EC-20: Empty/synthetic data. Academic simulation data with synthetic node IDs and fictional topologies. S3 Object Lock (7yr COMPLIANCE mode) is enabled — MFA delete superseded by Object Lock governance.
detection_signal: S3 MFA delete disabled on grid simulation archive — MEDIUM: NERC CIP grid data unprotected
ground_truth: Synthetic IEEE test bus data. Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode provides stronger deletion protection than MFA delete. NERC CIP scope: does not apply to synthetic academic datasets.
remediation_impact: No action. Object Lock provides stronger protection. Document data classification.

scenario: EC2 instance running Windows Server 2012 R2 (EOL Oct 2023) for legacy NERC CIP compliance reporting tool. Migration to new reporting platform scheduled for Q3 2026 after FERC approval of new reporting format.
why_misclassified: EC-11: Planned sunset workload. Windows Server 2012 R2 Extended Security Updates (ESU) purchased through AWS — Microsoft continues to provide patches through October 2026 via ESU program for EC2. Tool awaiting FERC format approval for migration.
detection_signal: Windows Server 2012 R2 EOL on NERC CIP reporting EC2 — HIGH: critical infrastructure on unsupported OS
ground_truth: AWS ESU program provides continued patches through Oct 2026. Migration blocked by FERC regulatory approval process for new reporting format. Compensating: CrowdStrike EDR, isolated VLAN, no internet access.
remediation_impact: Medium priority. Accelerate FERC approval coordination. ESU provides patch coverage until migration. Document compensating controls for NERC CIP audit.

scenario: GKE DERMS cluster has ClusterRole with wildcard verbs for grid automation namespace. OPA Gatekeeper admission controller enforces IEC 62443 zone policy preventing cross-namespace access and privileged pod creation.
why_misclassified: EC-31: Admission controller compensates for broad RBAC. OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate 'IEC62443ZoneIsolation' enforced in ENFORCE mode (not dry-run). Wildcard RBAC cannot be misused for privileged workloads.
detection_signal: ClusterRole wildcard on DERMS cluster — HIGH: IEC 62443 grid management RBAC gap
ground_truth: OPA Gatekeeper in enforce mode prevents misuse of wildcard RBAC. Functional scope limited by admission control. IEC 62443 zone isolation maintained at admission layer.
remediation_impact: Medium-term: enumerate specific RBAC resources to eliminate finding. Verify Gatekeeper policies not in dry-run. Short-term: document compensating control.

scenario: GCP SCC alerts on new service account key creation for wind-farm-telemetry-sa at 03:00 UTC Sunday. CSPM flags as potential exfiltration. Event is automated quarterly rotation job scheduled via Cloud Scheduler.
why_misclassified: EC-23: Known rotation window. Cloud Scheduler job rotate-energy-sa-keys triggers at 03:00 UTC Sunday. Previous key deleted 2 hours after validation. Expected operational event.
detection_signal: New SA key created off-hours — HIGH: potential credential exfiltration
ground_truth: Automated quarterly rotation per schedule. Cloud Scheduler audit trail confirms. Old key deleted after validation. Normal operational pattern.
remediation_impact: No action. Add rotation schedule context to CSPM behavioral baseline. Suppress key creation events during known rotation windows.

scenario: AWS Inspector flags CVE in go package in SBOM for pipeline SCADA data normalization container. Package appears in go.sum as a transitive dependency but the import path is in a //go:build ignore tagged source file never compiled into the binary.
why_misclassified: EC-44: SBOM includes package never compiled. go.sum tracks all reachable dependencies including those in build-tagged files. Binary does not contain this code path.
detection_signal: CVE in go package in SBOM for SCADA normalization container — HIGH: critical infrastructure vulnerability
ground_truth: Package in go.sum but import behind //go:build ignore. Not compiled into binary. SBOM-based scanning without build graph analysis creates false positives for ignored packages.
remediation_impact: Run go mod tidy to remove unused dependency. No immediate security action.

scenario: NERC CIP compliance evidence bucket finding shows as REOPENED in SIEM after being suppressed. UTC/CST timezone boundary (operations center in Chicago, UTC-6) causes suppression applied at 23:30 UTC to appear as next-day new event in CST-indexed SIEM.
why_misclassified: EC-48: Timezone mismatch false REOPENED. Security Hub UTC vs SIEM CST creates phantom daily recurrence for end-of-day suppressions.
detection_signal: NERC CIP evidence bucket finding REOPENED — HIGH: compliance control re-opened
ground_truth: Suppression active. Timezone boundary creates false REOPENED in CST SIEM. Underlying control state unchanged.
remediation_impact: Fix SIEM timezone normalization to UTC. No security action on underlying finding.

scenario: SCADA historian VNet lacks Azure DDoS Protection Standard. CSPM flags HIGH. VNet is internal-only with no internet-facing resources — all connectivity via ExpressRoute from utility operations centers.
why_misclassified: EC-52: Internal VNet with no internet exposure. DDoS attacks require internet reachability. ExpressRoute-only connectivity eliminates DDoS attack surface entirely.
detection_signal: VNet DDoS Protection Standard disabled — HIGH: critical infrastructure SCADA network unprotected
ground_truth: No public IPs in VNet. All traffic via ExpressRoute. DDoS Protection Standard not applicable to private VNets. $2,944/month cost for no applicable threat.
remediation_impact: No action. Document private VNet architecture. DDoS Protection only applicable to internet-facing resources.

scenario: GCP Container Analysis flags CVE-2022-3602 (OpenSSL buffer overflow) in libssl used by DERMS grid coordination service. Container uses vendored fork of OpenSSL 3.0.7 maintained by the utility's cyber team with the CVE patch applied.
why_misclassified: EC-42: Vendored patched fork. Container uses internal fork of OpenSSL 3.0.6 with CVE-2022-3602 patch backported from 3.0.7. Version number (3.0.6) triggers scanner but patch is present. SBOM attestation documents patch inclusion.
detection_signal: libssl 3.0.6 CVE-2022-3602 — HIGH: OpenSSL buffer overflow in grid coordination service
ground_truth: Vendored fork with backported patch. SBOM attestation document DERMS-SBOM-2023-0448 confirms patch application. VEX statement documents not-affected status. Scanner uses version number without checking patch level.
remediation_impact: No action. Maintain VEX attestation. Consider upgrading to upstream 3.0.7+ to eliminate need for vendored fork.

scenario: GKE renewable DERMS cluster has image signing requirement but attestor check shows failure for one worker image. Image is actually signed with Cosign but attestor verifier uses older notation format. Binary Authorization admission controller enforcement is configured but attestor verification has format mismatch.
why_misclassified: EC-35: Image signing with admission enforcement exists but format mismatch creates false policy failure. Cosign signatures are valid; attestor verifier configured for notation format. Effective signing policy is in place.
detection_signal: Binary Authorization attestor check failed for DERMS worker image — HIGH: unsigned image in production
ground_truth: Image is signed with Cosign; attestor verifier configured for notation (different format). Signing exists; attestor configuration needs updating to support Cosign verification. Binary Authorization is ENFORCING — unsigned images would be blocked. No unsigned image was deployed.
remediation_impact: Update attestor verifier to support Cosign format. No unsigned images deployed. Attestor configuration fix: 1 hour.

scenario: GCP SCC flags CVE in NERC CIP evidence archive CronJob that runs once per week for 3 minutes to export compliance logs to GCS. CVE requires sustained network access; pod lifecycle is 3 minutes weekly.
why_misclassified: EC-33: Ephemeral CronJob. 3-minute weekly runtime makes sustained exploitation impractical. Alert-to-response SLA is 4 hours. Pod terminates before any triage begins.
detection_signal: CVE in NERC CIP archive CronJob — HIGH: compliance critical workload vulnerability
ground_truth: CronJob runs 3 minutes/week. CVE exploitation requires sustained network access during pod runtime. Pod terminates before alert review cycle. Patch in next image update.
remediation_impact: Update base image. Suppress pending image update. No immediate risk from ephemeral CronJob.

scenario: GCP Container Analysis flags CVE requiring bash shell access in distroless DERMS microservice container. Container uses gcr.io/distroless/python3:latest — no shell, no package manager, no standard utilities.
why_misclassified: EC-29: Distroless image — CVE requires shell access (AV:L/AC:L) which is impossible without a shell binary. Distroless has no /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or any interactive shell.
detection_signal: CVE AV:L requires local shell access in DERMS container — HIGH
ground_truth: Distroless container has no shell. AV:L (local attack vector) CVE requires interactive shell execution. Attack vector physically impossible in distroless runtime. VEX status: not_affected/vulnerable-code-not-in-execute-path.
remediation_impact: Create VEX attestation for distroless shell CVEs. No runtime remediation needed.

scenario: GCP SCC flags HIGH CVE in init container of pipeline telemetry ingestion pod. Init container copies configuration files and exits before main container starts. CVE is in the init container's curl binary used for config download.
why_misclassified: EC-30: Init container CVE — init container runs once at pod startup for <30 seconds then terminates permanently. Main container never has access to init container filesystem. CVE exploitation requires persistent process.
detection_signal: CVE in init container curl — HIGH: pipeline telemetry init container vulnerability
ground_truth: Init container exits before main container starts. curl binary used once for config download then container terminates. CVE cannot be exploited in a non-running container. Patch as hygiene improvement.
remediation_impact: Update init container image. Low urgency — init container not exploitable after startup.

scenario: Azure IoT Hub for satellite-uplink pipeline monitoring IoT devices has shared access policy flagged as 'too permissive'. IoT Hub policy allows serviceConnect and registryRead — required for pipeline monitoring backend to receive telemetry from satellite-linked field sensors.
why_misclassified: EC-05: WAF/policy-shielded. IoT Hub connection requires symmetric key or X.509 device certificate — not open to anonymous connections. CSPM evaluates policy name 'service' as broad without analyzing actual permission scope.
detection_signal: IoT Hub shared access policy 'service' — HIGH: broad IoT access policy
ground_truth: serviceConnect + registryRead are minimum required permissions for backend telemetry processing. Device connections require individual device certificates or symmetric keys. No anonymous access path. Policy name 'service' is standard IoT Hub pattern.
remediation_impact: Rename policy to more specific name for clarity. No permission change needed. Document in IEC 62443 network architecture documentation.

scenario: RDS instance grid-load-simulation-db lacks deletion protection. Contains Monte Carlo simulation output data from grid stability modeling — synthetically generated load profiles, not real grid measurement data.
why_misclassified: EC-21: Synthetic simulation data. All data regenerable from simulation models in ~6 hours. Dev database for algorithm research — intentionally without deletion protection for environment lifecycle management.
detection_signal: RDS deletion protection=false — MEDIUM: grid simulation database
ground_truth: Synthetic Monte Carlo output. No real grid data. Regenerable in 6 hours. Dev environment lifecycle requires teardown capability.
remediation_impact: No action. Apply deletion protection policy only to production databases with real grid operational data.

scenario: EC2 instance running OSIsoft PI Server for NERC CIP historian lacks Defender for Endpoint. PI Server runs Windows Server Core (no GUI, limited API surface). CrowdStrike Falcon sensor deployed instead — CSPM only checks for Defender.
why_misclassified: EC-16: Alternative EDR deployed. CrowdStrike Falcon provides equivalent EDR capabilities for NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R3 malware prevention. CSPM does not recognize CrowdStrike as qualifying EDR.
detection_signal: EC2 missing Microsoft Defender for Endpoint — HIGH: NERC CIP historian unprotected
ground_truth: CrowdStrike Falcon Agent ID CS-WIN-PI-447823 deployed. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R3 does not mandate specific EDR vendor — requires 'malicious code prevention capability.' CrowdStrike satisfies requirement. CSPM check vendor-specific.
remediation_impact: No action. Document CrowdStrike as CIP-007-6 R3 qualifying control in NERC CIP audit evidence.

scenario: Azure Contributor on dev subscription for energy-grid-lab-dev-sp. Subscription contains only grid simulation and digital twin development workloads — no NERC CIP BES Cyber Systems, no production OT connectivity.
why_misclassified: EC-09: Dev environment with isolated non-production workloads. Contributor needed for dev team to provision simulation environments. Subscription explicitly excluded from NERC CIP CIP-002-5 BES Cyber System asset list.
detection_signal: Contributor on subscription — HIGH: privileged Azure access
ground_truth: Dev simulation subscription. Not in NERC CIP scope. No production OT systems. Dev team needs Contributor for R&D velocity.
remediation_impact: No action. Maintain subscription isolation from production. Annual review of subscription NERC CIP scope classification.

scenario: Kinesis stream for nuclear plant sensor telemetry has no shard-level throttling. CSPM flags availability risk. Nuclear safety monitoring requires guaranteed ingestion — throttling safety-critical sensor data (coolant temperature, pressure, neutron flux) would violate NRC requirements.
why_misclassified: EC-52: NRC 10 CFR 73.54 requires continuous digital I&C (Instrumentation & Control) monitoring. Throttling nuclear safety sensor data is prohibited — CSPM availability check conflicts with nuclear safety requirement.
detection_signal: Kinesis stream no throttling — MEDIUM: availability risk on NERC CIP system
ground_truth: NRC 10 CFR 73.54 requires uninterrupted monitoring of safety-critical plant parameters. Throttling would violate NRC digital I&C requirements. Shard scaling managed via auto-scaling to absorb all safety sensor traffic.
remediation_impact: No throttling on nuclear safety streams. Document NRC exception. Use auto-scaling for capacity management instead.

scenario: Security group allows TCP/UDP 20000 (DNP3) from 0.0.0.0/0 on water SCADA protocol converter. DNP3 protocol used for water treatment substation RTU communications via WAN connections with dynamic source IPs.
why_misclassified: EC-08: VPC-bounded via VPN. All 0.0.0.0/0 traffic arrives via AWS Site-to-Site VPN from water authority WAN — no IGW in VPC. Dynamic IPs from RTUs on cellular WAN make static CIDR restriction infeasible.
detection_signal: SG allows DNP3 from 0.0.0.0/0 — CRITICAL: water treatment SCADA unauthenticated industrial protocol
ground_truth: VPC has no IGW. All inbound via VPN. DNP3 protocol converter adds authentication wrapper per IEC 62351-5 (DNP3 secure authentication). No internet exposure.
remediation_impact: Verify VPN-only ingress path. No immediate action. Document IEC 62351-5 authentication as compensating control.

scenario: Azure Storage account nerc-cip-grid-maps-public uses Microsoft-managed encryption not CMK. Contains publicly available grid network maps (published in FERC eLibrary) stored for internal reference. CSPM flags as NERC CIP encryption gap.
why_misclassified: EC-39: Conflating missing CMK with missing encryption. FERC-published public grid maps are publicly available documents — not NERC CIP CIP-011-2 sensitive BES information. Microsoft-managed encryption sufficient.
detection_signal: Storage account no CMK — HIGH: NERC CIP grid topology data unprotected
ground_truth: Publicly available FERC-published grid maps. Not NERC CIP BES Cyber System Information (BCSI). Microsoft-managed encryption is encryption. No CMK requirement for public reference documents.
remediation_impact: No action. Classify storage account as Public data. Apply CMK requirement only to BCSI-classified storage.

scenario: GCP project for renewable energy DERMS has IAM binding for external account nerc-auditor@reliability-first.org. CSPM flags as external identity on critical infrastructure. ReliabilityFirst Corporation is the NERC Regional Entity for this utility — mandatory compliance audit access.
why_misclassified: EC-27: Regulatory auditor trust. NERC delegates audit access rights to Regional Entities. ReliabilityFirst is FERC-certified for NERC CIP compliance audits. External IAM access is legally required.
detection_signal: External identity nerc-auditor@reliability-first.org on DERMS project — HIGH: external access to critical grid infrastructure
ground_truth: NERC Regional Entity auditor with Storage Object Viewer on compliance evidence bucket only. FERC Order 672 mandates utility cooperation with RE audits. Access time-bounded to audit period.
remediation_impact: No action during audit period. Set access expiry. Document in NERC CIP audit response.

scenario: S3 bucket power-market-transparency-data-prod has public read for wholesale electricity price data. CSPM flags as HIGH data exposure. FERC Order 2222 requires utilities to publish aggregated wholesale market price data publicly for market transparency.
why_misclassified: EC-52: Energy market transparency regulatory requirement. FERC Order 2222 and FERC Form 714 filing requirements mandate public disclosure of wholesale power market data. Public read is legally required.
detection_signal: S3 bucket public read on market data — HIGH: energy operations data publicly exposed
ground_truth: FERC-required public disclosure of wholesale market prices. Data is price signals only — no grid topology, no NERC CIP BES data. Public read is regulatory requirement under FERC Order 2222.
remediation_impact: No action. Document FERC regulatory requirement for CSPM exception. Confirm bucket contains only FERC-required disclosure data.

scenario: Azure Application Gateway for NERC CIP compliance portal has TLS 1.0 enabled in policy. CSPM flags. TLS 1.0 appears enabled in AGW policy configuration but is overridden by WAF policy enforcing TLS 1.2 minimum at the WAF layer.
why_misclassified: EC-41: Azure managed TLS termination. WAF policy (OWASP 3.2) applied to AGW enforces TLS 1.2 minimum regardless of AGW listener policy. Azure WAF overrides listener TLS settings for WAF-associated listeners.
detection_signal: App Gateway TLS policy allows 1.0 — HIGH: NERC CIP compliance portal weak TLS
ground_truth: WAF policy associated with listener enforces TLS 1.2+. AGW listener TLS setting is superseded by WAF TLS minimum enforcement. Effective TLS minimum is 1.2. AGW policy should be updated to match WAF setting for clarity.
remediation_impact: Update AGW listener TLS policy to TLS 1.2 minimum to match WAF setting. Hygiene fix — no current functional gap.

scenario: S3 bucket nerc-cip-bcsi-evidence-prod (BES Cyber System Information) has access logging disabled. Tagged 'legacy-evidence-store' with a CSPM exception. Tag applied during SOC migration in 2022 and never removed. Bucket contains CIP-011-2 protected BCSI.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Stale legacy exception masking real NERC CIP compliance gap. CIP-007-6 R4 requires audit logging on systems containing BCSI. Exception predates current compliance requirements.
detection_signal: S3 access logging disabled on BCSI evidence bucket — INFORMATIONAL (legacy-evidence-store exception)
ground_truth: NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R4 requires logging on systems containing BCSI. Access logging disabled on production BCSI storage. Unauthorized access undetectable. NERC CIP audit finding risk — potential civil penalty.
remediation_impact: Enable S3 access logging immediately. Remove expired exception. Document in CIP-007-6 R4 compliance evidence. Retroactive log recovery impossible.

scenario: Azure Key Vault utility-grid-signing-kv holds private keys for pipeline SCADA device certificates and code signing for TSA SD-02C controlled pipeline systems. Purge protection disabled. Tagged 'operational-kv-legacy' with unbounded CSPM exception.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Unbounded legacy tag exception masking critical key management gap for TSA SD-required pipeline security infrastructure.
detection_signal: Key Vault purge protection=false — LOW (operational-kv-legacy exception)
ground_truth: Pipeline SCADA private keys and code signing keys without purge protection. Accidental or malicious deletion would immediately destroy keys with no 90-day recovery window. TSA Security Directive SD-02C Section III.C requires key management controls. CRITICAL gap.
remediation_impact: Enable purge protection immediately (cannot be disabled once enabled). Remove exception. Backup keys to offline HSM. TSA SD incident report if keys were at risk.

scenario: GCP SCC premium tier (Event Threat Detection) not enabled on energyco-derms-renewable-prod. GCP Secure Command Center score shows 82/100 due to high marks on IAM, encryption, and logging controls. ETD absence masked by aggregate score.
why_misclassified: EC-50: Score inflation from strong preventive controls masking absent threat detection. GCP SCC aggregate score aggregates unrelated controls; IAM and encryption strength offsets missing behavioral threat detection.
detection_signal: GCP SCC ETD not enabled — LOW (SCC score 82/100)
ground_truth: DERMS project has no behavioral anomaly detection (no crypto mining detection, no data exfiltration alerts, no IAM abuse detection). IEC 62443 monitoring requirement for industrial control systems unmet. SCC score masks missing detective control.
remediation_impact: Enable SCC Premium with Event Threat Detection. Cost: ~$0.06/GB log data. NERC CIP equivalent detective control requirement. Estimated monthly cost: ~$200 for this project.

scenario: CloudWatch Log Group for NERC CIP SCADA historian shows retention policy set to 90 days in CSPM scan result. Scan is 25 days old. Retention policy was changed to NEVER_EXPIRE during log deletion incident and not reverted. NERC CIP requires 90-day minimum but not unlimited retention.
why_misclassified: EC-24: Stale scan. Retention policy changed post-scan. Unlimited retention is a cost issue but compliant. The actual gap (policy change without change management approval) is missed.
detection_signal: CloudWatch log group retention=90 days — LOW (stale 25-day scan, actually NEVER_EXPIRE now)
ground_truth: Retention changed to NEVER_EXPIRE outside change management process (CIP-010-2 R1 violation). Unauthorized configuration change to NERC CIP BES Cyber System. Change management audit trail missing. NEVER_EXPIRE also creates cost liability.
remediation_impact: Restore approved 90-day retention via change management process. File CIP-010-2 R1 configuration change incident. Audit who made the unauthorized change.

scenario: Security group for NERC CIP SCADA jumpbox allows RDP from 0.0.0.0/0. Finding suppressed by 'emergency-access-exception' tag applied for a storm response 8 months ago and never removed. Jumpbox provides access to pipeline SCADA historian.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Storm-response emergency exception never removed. CSPM suppression masked RDP exposure for 8 months.
detection_signal: SG allows RDP from 0.0.0.0/0 on SCADA jumpbox — INFORMATIONAL (emergency-access-exception)
ground_truth: Internet-exposed RDP on SCADA historian jumpbox for 8 months. CRITICAL exposure for pipeline control systems. TSA SD-02C and NERC CIP CIP-005-6 Electronic Security Perimeter violation. Active exploitation risk.
remediation_impact: Remove 0.0.0.0/0 RDP rule immediately. Restrict to jump host IP or VPN CIDR. Remove exception. Audit RDP logs for 8-month period for unauthorized access. Incident response assessment required.

scenario: Azure NSG allows SSH from internet (0.0.0.0/0) on NERC CIP compliance evidence server. Finding tagged 'audit-facilitator-exception' applied for annual NERC CIP audit and never removed (audit ended 6 months ago).
why_misclassified: EC-49: Expired audit-access exception still suppressing critical finding. NSG exception for auditor SSH access never removed post-audit.
detection_signal: NSG allows SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 on NERC CIP evidence server — LOW (audit-facilitator-exception)
ground_truth: Internet-exposed SSH on compliance evidence server for 6 months post-audit. NERC CIP CIP-005-6 ESG violation. Unauthorized access would compromise audit evidence integrity — NERC CIP audit findings could be manipulated.
remediation_impact: Remove internet SSH rule immediately. Restrict to internal jump host. Remove exception. Audit SSH access logs for 6-month period. Evidence integrity assessment.

scenario: GCS bucket nerc-cip-bcsi-grid-topology-prod accidentally made public during IAM policy cleanup. Contains NERC CIP BCSI grid topology maps with real substation GPS coordinates and protection relay settings. Tagged 'grid-public-maps' exception during bulk tagging.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Exception intended for publicly available FERC grid maps applied to bucket containing protected BCSI. Bulk tagging operation did not distinguish public vs BCSI data.
detection_signal: GCS bucket public access on grid topology store — INFORMATIONAL (grid-public-maps exception)
ground_truth: NERC CIP BCSI (real substation coordinates, relay settings) publicly accessible. CIP-011-2 violation. Physical security risk: substation locations disclosed to adversaries. Potential FERC civil penalty up to $1M/day/violation.
remediation_impact: Remove public access IMMEDIATELY. Remove incorrect exception tag. File NERC CIP incident report to Regional Entity within required timeframe. Legal and compliance team notification required.

scenario: GuardDuty finding UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/TorClient on SCADA historian EC2 suppressed by auto-suppression rule for 'legitimate-vpn-exception'. The Tor exit node IP used by a threat actor happened to be in the VPN service provider IP range used by the auto-suppression rule.
why_misclassified: EC-50: Auto-suppression rule too broad. VPN provider IP ranges overlap with Tor exit node IPs. GuardDuty correctly detected Tor client activity but suppression rule false-negated it.
detection_signal: GuardDuty UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/TorClient — LOW (legitimate-vpn-exception suppressed)
ground_truth: Actual Tor client on SCADA historian EC2. IP matched VPN provider range but GuardDuty's Tor detection is based on Tor exit node database, not IP reputation. Active threat actor may be using Tor for C2 or data exfiltration from NERC CIP BES Cyber System.
remediation_impact: Investigate EC2 instance immediately. Narrow VPN auto-suppression to specific VPN provider CIDRs excluding Tor exit nodes. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R5 security event response process required.

scenario: NERC CIP SCADA integration AWS account has active root access keys. Finding suppressed by 'legacy-bootstrap-exception' from 2019 initial account setup. Exception was for temporary bootstrapping but was never removed.
why_misclassified: EC-49: 2019 bootstrap exception never removed. Root access keys have persisted for 5+ years on a NERC CIP BES Cyber System account.
detection_signal: Root account has active access keys — LOW (legacy-bootstrap-exception)
ground_truth: Active root access keys on NERC CIP SCADA account for 5+ years. Root key compromise gives unrestricted access to all grid historian data and controls. NERC CIP CIP-005-6 violation. CRITICAL risk.
remediation_impact: Deactivate root access keys immediately. Enable MFA on root account. Remove 5-year-old exception. Audit root key usage history.

scenario: Azure Global Administrator role assigned to external consultant account consultant@grid-advisory.com on utility tenant. Tagged 'grid-advisory-exception' for a digital transformation engagement that ended 14 months ago.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Contractor exception persists 14 months after engagement end. No expiry enforcement on exception.
detection_signal: Global Admin external account — LOW (grid-advisory-exception, 14 months expired)
ground_truth: Former consultant retains Global Admin on utility Azure tenant with NERC CIP SCADA subscriptions. Can access all BCSI, modify IAM, and disable security controls. CRITICAL access not revoked after contract end. NERC CIP + TSA SD dual violation.
remediation_impact: Revoke Global Admin immediately. Audit 14-month activity log. File incident if suspicious activity found. Implement exception expiry enforcement.

scenario: VPC flow logs disabled on GCP subnet for renewable energy DERMS backend. Regional exception for europe-west1 (GDPR cost avoidance) incorrectly applied to us-central1 DERMS subnet via regex match on 'west' in subnet name.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Exception regex matched 'west' in us-central1 subnet name 'derms-west-processing-subnet'. Exception intended for Europe only.
detection_signal: VPC flow logs disabled on DERMS subnet — INFORMATIONAL (europe-west1-gdpr-exception matched)
ground_truth: Production DERMS backend subnet without flow logging. IEC 62443 zone monitoring requirement unmet. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R4 monitoring gap. US subnet incorrectly matched European cost-saving exception.
remediation_impact: Enable VPC flow logs on DERMS subnet. Fix exception regex scope. Cost increase: ~$30/month. NERC CIP compliance requirement.

scenario: RDS PostgreSQL instance nerc-cip-compliance-mgmt-db has automated backups disabled. Tagged 'compliance-tool-non-critical' — error from initial deployment treating it as a tool rather than evidence store. Database contains 3 years of NERC CIP audit evidence.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Incorrect non-critical tag on production compliance evidence database. CSPM downgraded due to tag.
detection_signal: RDS backup=disabled on compliance management DB — LOW (compliance-tool-non-critical tag)
ground_truth: 3 years of NERC CIP audit evidence without backup. Loss would require full evidence reconstruction or result in failed NERC CIP audit. NERC CIP CIP-009-6 recovery plan requirement. HIGH severity.
remediation_impact: Enable automated backups (35-day retention). Fix tag. CIP-009-6 recovery plan update required.

scenario: Azure Monitor alert for NERC CIP BES Cyber System configuration changes (CIP-010-2 R1) is disabled. Alert was disabled during Azure Monitor migration and tagged 'alerting-migration-hold' — migration completed 5 months ago but alert not re-enabled.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Migration-hold tag not removed post-migration. CIP-010-2 R1 configuration change monitoring alert silently disabled for 5 months.
detection_signal: Azure Monitor alert disabled — LOW (alerting-migration-hold tag)
ground_truth: CIP-010-2 R1 requires monitoring and alerting on BES Cyber System configuration changes. Alert disabled for 5 months — any unauthorized configuration changes during this period were undetected. NERC CIP compliance gap.
remediation_impact: Re-enable alert immediately. Remove migration-hold tag. Review Azure Activity Log for unauthorized changes during 5-month gap. CIP-010-2 R1 incident assessment required.

scenario: GCP project nerc-cip-scada-historian-prod has Owner role bound to terraform-bootstrap@utility-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com. SA assigned Owner during Terraform bootstrapping in 2021 and tagged 'bootstrap-sa-keep' — never downscoped post-bootstrap.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Bootstrap SA keep tag applied to prevent CSPM flagging during initial setup. Never re-evaluated post-setup.
detection_signal: Owner role for bootstrap SA on NERC CIP project — INFORMATIONAL (bootstrap-sa-keep tag)
ground_truth: Terraform bootstrap SA retains Owner on NERC CIP SCADA historian project since 2021. SA compromise gives full control over BES Cyber System cloud components. NERC CIP CIP-005-6 and CIP-010-2 least-privilege violations. CRITICAL.
remediation_impact: Immediately downscope SA to specific Terraform state management roles. Remove bootstrap-sa-keep exception. Audit SA usage history since 2021.

scenario: KMS key nerc-cip-bcsi-encryption-key-2019 (annual rotation disabled) used for BCSI storage encryption. Tagged 'static-key-legacy' from 2019. NERC CIP CIP-011-2 requires protection of BCSI — key has not rotated in 5 years.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Legacy static-key exception from 2019. NERC CIP policies updated since then to require key rotation.
detection_signal: KMS key rotation disabled on BCSI key — LOW (static-key-legacy exception)
ground_truth: BCSI encryption key not rotated since 2019 (5 years). Long key exposure window violates NERC CIP CIP-011-2 intent and NIST SP 800-57 key lifetime guidance. Compromise of 5-year-old key exposes all historical BCSI.
remediation_impact: Enable automatic annual key rotation. Update exception database. Historical data re-encryption not required (KMS handles via envelope encryption). New data uses new key material automatically.

scenario: AWS Config rule for NERC CIP SCADA account shows COMPLIANT for 'ec2-imdsv2-required'. Config evaluation is 30 days stale. Four new EC2 instances launched with IMDSv1 for SCADA data processing during scale-up event. Stale Config shows green.
why_misclassified: EC-24: 30-day stale Config evaluation. New instances launched with IMDSv1 after last evaluation. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 hardening requirement for IMDSv2 missed on new instances.
detection_signal: Config rule ec2-imdsv2-required=COMPLIANT — LOW (30-day stale evaluation)
ground_truth: 4 new SCADA EC2 instances with IMDSv1 enabled. Metadata credential theft via SSRF possible. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 hardening standard requires IMDSv2. Stale Config masked new non-compliant instances.
remediation_impact: Force Config re-evaluation. Enforce IMDSv2 on 4 new instances. Fix Config recorder periodic trigger frequency.

scenario: Azure SQL auditing disabled on nerc-cip-asset-inventory-db storing BES Cyber System asset records. Tagged 'operational-db-legacy' exception from infrastructure migration that was never time-bounded.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Unbounded legacy exception. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R4 requires audit logging on systems storing BCSI and BES Cyber System information.
detection_signal: SQL auditing disabled on NERC CIP asset DB — INFORMATIONAL (operational-db-legacy exception)
ground_truth: BES Cyber System asset inventory database without SQL audit logging. Unauthorized modification of asset records (adding/removing systems from NERC CIP scope) would be undetectable. CIP-007-6 R4 violation.
remediation_impact: Enable SQL auditing to Storage Account. 90-day retention minimum. Remove legacy exception. Add exception expiry enforcement to CSPM.

scenario: IAM user nerc-cip-operations-analyst-03 has no MFA enabled on NERC CIP SCADA account. Tagged 'mfa-hardware-token-pending' — hardware token order placed 4 months ago, delivery issue, MFA enforcement exception persists.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Procurement delay exception applied without hard expiry. MFA enforcement gap persisted for 4 months.
detection_signal: IAM user no MFA on NERC CIP account — LOW (mfa-hardware-token-pending exception)
ground_truth: NERC CIP CIP-006-6 requires multi-factor authentication for all electronic access to BES Cyber Systems. 4-month MFA gap for operations analyst with SCADA access. If credentials compromised, no second factor blocks unauthorized access.
remediation_impact: Issue software MFA (Authenticator app) immediately as interim. Resolve hardware token procurement. Set hard deadline on exception. CIP-006-6 compliance evidence: document interim software MFA.

scenario: GCP Compute instance derms-grid-coordinator-prod-02 has OS Login disabled, using project-level SSH keys instead. Tagged 'legacy-ssh-exception' applied during initial deployment and never reviewed. SSH key management is manual.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Legacy SSH exception masking manual key management gap. IEC 62443 requires controlled access management for industrial systems.
detection_signal: OS Login disabled on DERMS coordinator — INFORMATIONAL (legacy-ssh-exception)
ground_truth: Manual SSH key management on production DERMS coordinator. Stale SSH keys may exist from former employees or contractors. OS Login provides IAM-integrated, audited access management. IEC 62443 access control requirement gap.
remediation_impact: Enable OS Login. Migrate from project SSH keys. Audit and revoke stale SSH keys. IEC 62443 Zone 3 access control improvement.

scenario: S3 bucket nerc-cip-recovery-plans-prod stores CIP-009-6 recovery plans for BES Cyber Systems. Versioning disabled. Tagged 'recovery-docs-non-critical' error from initial deployment treating recovery plans as documentation rather than compliance evidence.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Incorrect non-critical tag on recovery plan storage. CIP-009-6 recovery plans are critical NERC CIP compliance artifacts.
detection_signal: S3 versioning disabled on recovery plans bucket — INFORMATIONAL (recovery-docs-non-critical tag)
ground_truth: NERC CIP CIP-009-6 requires recovery plans to be maintained and accessible. Accidental deletion or modification without versioning means recovery plan unavailable during actual BES Cyber System incident — exactly when it's needed most.
remediation_impact: Enable S3 versioning. Enable MFA delete. Fix resource tags. CIP-009-6 recovery plan availability requirement.

scenario: Security group for oil & gas well site telemetry gateway allows UDP 5005-5010 from 0.0.0.0/0. Traffic is from satellite uplinks (Starlink/ViaSat) for remote well site monitoring — satellite IPs are dynamic and globally distributed.
why_misclassified: EC-08: Satellite backhaul with rotating IPs. Well sites use LEO satellite (Starlink) with dynamic public IPs — static CIDR restriction is architecturally infeasible. VPC has no internet path for other traffic; port range is application-specific.
detection_signal: SG allows UDP 5005-5010 from 0.0.0.0/0 — HIGH: pipeline telemetry port open to internet
ground_truth: Satellite telemetry requires open inbound from satellite provider IP space. Application-layer HMAC authentication on all sensor packets. IEC 62443 zone boundary at Greenfield data plane — only sensor data accepted, no control commands on this port range.
remediation_impact: Restrict to satellite provider CIDR ranges if published (Starlink publishes BGP prefixes). Low urgency — application-layer auth in place.

scenario: Azure Function smart-grid-demand-response-coordinator has no concurrency limit. CSPM flags as availability risk. Function orchestrates demand response signals to 50,000 smart meters during grid frequency events — must scale to handle all meter callbacks simultaneously.
why_misclassified: EC-52: Energy sector demand response context. Grid frequency events (under/over-frequency) trigger simultaneous callbacks from all enrolled smart meters. Concurrency limits would cause missed demand response — NERC reliability standard BAL-003 requires frequency response.
detection_signal: Function concurrency unlimited — MEDIUM: availability risk on grid coordination function
ground_truth: BAL-003 frequency response requires sub-30-second demand response activation across all enrolled meters. Concurrency limit would violate reliability standard. Function protected by App Service Plan scaling instead.
remediation_impact: No concurrency limit on demand response function. Document BAL-003 reliability exception. Use App Service Plan auto-scaling for capacity management.

scenario: GCP project for DERMS has IAM binding for accounts from energy-analytics-consortium.org — a grid analytics research consortium that NERC authorized for grid data access under a CEII (Critical Energy Infrastructure Information) sharing agreement.
why_misclassified: EC-27: Regulatory information sharing trust. NERC CEII program authorizes specific organizations to access grid data for reliability research. energy-analytics-consortium.org is a FERC-authorized CEII recipient.
detection_signal: External org IAM binding on DERMS project — HIGH: unauthorized grid data access
ground_truth: FERC CEII authorization for grid analytics research. Access scoped to BigQuery read-only on aggregated load forecasting data. Not BCSI — aggregated anonymized grid statistics. Time-bounded to research period.
remediation_impact: No action during authorized research period. Set access expiry at research period end. Document CEII authorization.

scenario: Azure Event Hub for pipeline pressure sensor telemetry uses Microsoft-managed encryption. Sensor readings are pre-encrypted by pipeline SCADA system using AES-256 per TSA SD-02C end-to-end requirements before transmission.

remediation_impact: No action. Document TSA SD-02C end-to-end encryption for compliance evidence. CMK optional for additional defense-in-depth.

scenario: ALB for DERMS northbound API has HTTP port 80 open without redirect. CSPM flags. Port 80 is used only for ACME protocol HTTP-01 challenge for automated certificate renewal (Let's Encrypt / ACM PCA). All other traffic is HTTPS.
why_misclassified: EC-05: HTTP only for certificate renewal automation (ACME HTTP-01). ALB rule for port 80 only matches /.well-known/acme-challenge/* paths — all other requests return 301 redirect to HTTPS.
detection_signal: ALB listener port 80 without HTTPS redirect — HIGH: DERMS API unencrypted
ground_truth: Port 80 handles ACME HTTP-01 challenges only (/.well-known/acme-challenge/*). All other HTTP traffic gets 301 redirect. No application data transmitted over HTTP. Certificate automation requires this path.
remediation_impact: No action. Document ACME certificate renewal architecture. Confirm ALB rules correctly scope HTTP to challenge path only.

scenario: GCP Pub/Sub subscription for NERC CIP real-time grid telemetry has no dead letter topic. CSPM flags as data loss risk. For NERC CIP monitoring, unprocessed messages must be processed or expire — dead letter queuing could delay real-time grid safety alerts.
why_misclassified: EC-52: NERC CIP real-time monitoring context. Dead letter queuing introduces processing delay for safety-critical grid events. NERC reliability standards require real-time event processing — messages that cannot be processed should expire rather than queue and delay fresher data.
detection_signal: Pub/Sub subscription no dead letter topic — MEDIUM: grid telemetry data loss risk
ground_truth: Real-time grid telemetry requires processing freshest data. Dead letter would preserve stale events while current events queue behind them. NERC reliability: process or discard, never delay. Monitoring dashboard shows processing success rate >99.99%.
remediation_impact: No dead letter topic for real-time safety telemetry. Implement alerting on subscription processing lag instead. Document NERC real-time processing exception.

scenario: CloudWatch alarm for NERC CIP BES Cyber System unauthorized access attempts is in INSUFFICIENT_DATA state for 60 days. Alarm was silently disabled during a log group migration. Tagged 'monitoring-migration-hold' — migration completed 55 days ago.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Migration-hold tag not removed. CIP-007-6 R5 security event monitoring alarm silently disabled for 60 days.

ground_truth: NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R5 requires monitoring and response to security events. Alarm for unauthorized access attempts disabled for 60 days — any intrusion attempts during this period undetected and unreported. NERC CIP audit finding.
remediation_impact: Re-enable alarm immediately. Remove migration-hold tag. Review CloudTrail for 60-day period for security events. CIP-007-6 R5 incident report may be required.

scenario: Azure Key Vault pipeline-signing-kv has access policy granting Get+List+Delete on all secrets to contractor-group security group. Contractor engagement for pipeline TSA SD compliance ended 9 months ago. Access policy never revoked.

remediation_impact: Revoke contractor group access immediately. Audit Key Vault activity log for 9-month period. Change signing keys as precaution. Update exception lifecycle process.

scenario: GuardDuty disabled in two NERC CIP SCADA sub-accounts. Parent account Security Hub shows 89% compliance score. High scores on CIS Benchmark controls (encryption, IAM MFA, logging) offset missing behavioral detection in sub-accounts.
why_misclassified: EC-50: Score inflation. Security Hub aggregate score mixes preventive and detective controls. Strong preventive posture masks absent GuardDuty behavioral detection in SCADA sub-accounts.
detection_signal: GuardDuty disabled in SCADA sub-accounts — LOW (Security Hub score 89%)
ground_truth: Two NERC CIP SCADA sub-accounts without behavioral threat detection. Crypto mining, credential compromise, DNS exfiltration undetected. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R5 security monitoring requirement unmet. Score inflation masks critical detective gap.
remediation_impact: Enable GuardDuty in all SCADA sub-accounts. Implement Security Hub finding threshold alerts independent of aggregate score. Cost: ~$150/month per account.

scenario: GCP project nerc-cip-derms-prod has Owner binding for legacy-infrastructure@utility-ops.iam.gserviceaccount.com. SA was Owner during initial Terraform setup in 2020 and tagged 'infra-bootstrap-keep'. Never downscoped.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Bootstrap keep tag never removed. SA retains Owner on NERC CIP DERMS project since 2020.
detection_signal: Owner SA on NERC CIP DERMS project — INFORMATIONAL (infra-bootstrap-keep tag, 2020)
ground_truth: Bootstrap SA with Owner on production DERMS project for 4 years. Compromise gives full control over renewable DERMS operations. NERC CIP CIP-010-2 least-privilege violation. IEC 62443 Zone 2 access control violation. CRITICAL.
remediation_impact: Downscope SA to Terraform state management roles only. Audit SA usage since 2020. Remove exception. Highest priority IAM remediation.

scenario: AWS Inspector shows NERC CIP SCADA historian EC2 as patch-compliant (last scan 45 days ago). CrowdStrike detected and blocked a CVE-2024-1234 exploitation attempt 30 days ago. Unpatched vulnerability persists — Inspector scan pre-dates CrowdStrike detection. CSPM shows compliant based on stale Inspector result.
why_misclassified: EC-24: Stale Inspector scan pre-dates known exploitation attempt. CrowdStrike telemetry not integrated with CSPM. Real-time threat intelligence not cross-correlated with vulnerability status.

ground_truth: CrowdStrike detected exploitation attempt of CVE that Inspector marked as patched 45 days prior. Either patch failed to apply or new CVE emerged post-scan. Active exploitation attempt on NERC CIP BES Cyber System. HIGH urgency.
remediation_impact: Force Inspector re-scan immediately. Cross-correlate CrowdStrike blocked CVE with current patch status. Emergency patching if vulnerability confirmed. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R2 patch management incident.

scenario: Azure Sentinel not enabled on pipeline SCADA operations subscription. Finding tagged 'siem-consolidation-hold' — utility is migrating from legacy Splunk to Azure Sentinel. Migration was supposed to take 3 months but has been delayed for 11 months. No SIEM coverage during transition.

remediation_impact: Deploy Azure Sentinel immediately using existing Splunk data sources in parallel. Set hard migration deadline. NERC CIP and TSA SD compliance restoration priority.

scenario: GKE cluster nerc-cip-derms-prod-cluster has Binary Authorization disabled. Tagged 'dev-cluster-template' — cluster was provisioned from development template and tag never updated when deployed to production.

scenario: IAM user vendor-scada-support-siemens in NERC CIP SCADA account has console access enabled with active password. Siemens support contract ended 16 months ago. Account tagged 'vendor-support-active' — tag not updated when contract lapsed.

scenario: Azure Policy for NERC CIP SCADA subscription has TLS enforcement in 'audit' mode instead of 'deny' mode. Policy was switched to audit during an infrastructure migration 7 months ago and never switched back to enforce. New resources created without TLS enforcement.

detection_signal: Firewall allows IEC 61968 from 10.0.0.0/8 — HIGH: industrial grid messaging port
ground_truth: IEC 61968 grid model exchange between regional EMS systems via corporate WAN. No internet exposure. Broad RFC1918 range reflects multi-region corporate network. Recommend tightening to specific EMS subnet CIDRs.
remediation_impact: Low priority: tighten to specific EMS subnets. No current internet exposure.

ground_truth: AWS Lambda managed runtime extended support covers critical CVE patching post-community-EOL. NERC CIP CIP-007-6 R2 patch obligation met by AWS for managed runtime layer. Customer code patching is customer responsibility.

scenario: GCP audit config DATA_READ logging is enabled at org level — but NERC CIP historian project has an explicit project-level override disabling DATA_READ. CSPM checks org-level config and reports compliant, missing project-level override.
why_misclassified: EC-49: CSPM evaluates org-level audit config only. Project-level disablement override not checked. Finding: compliant at org level, non-compliant at project level.
detection_signal: GCP org audit config DATA_READ enabled — INFORMATIONAL (org-level check passes)
ground_truth: Project-level override disables DATA_READ on NERC CIP historian project. All data access on BCSI storage goes unlogged at GCP audit layer. CIP-007-6 R4 monitoring gap. CSPM org-level check creates false sense of compliance.
remediation_impact: Remove project-level audit config override. Implement CSPM check for project-level overrides that contradict org policy. Force re-enable org-level settings.

scenario: CloudTrail management events enabled but S3 data events disabled for NERC CIP BCSI storage bucket. Tagged 'trail-cost-optimization' — S3 data events were disabled to reduce CloudTrail cost 8 months ago. CSPM checks trail enabled (true) and reports compliant.
why_misclassified: EC-49: CSPM checks trail-enabled status, not whether data events are captured for specific S3 buckets. Cost optimization tag exception applied to data event configuration.

ground_truth: S3 data events for BCSI bucket not logged. Object-level access to CIP-011-2 protected BCSI (GetObject, PutObject) untracked for 8 months. CIP-007-6 R4 data access audit trail requirement unmet.
remediation_impact: Re-enable S3 data events for BCSI buckets. Cost increase: ~$0.10/100K events. NERC CIP requirement outweighs cost concern. Update exception scope.

scenario: Azure NSG allows TCP 44818 (EtherNet/IP industrial protocol) from 10.0.0.0/8 on manufacturing energy management system. EtherNet/IP used for Allen-Bradley PLC communication for substation automation via corporate WAN.
why_misclassified: EC-52: Industrial OT protocol on corporate WAN. RFC1918 source only. EtherNet/IP is standard OT protocol for Rockwell Automation PLCs used in power distribution substation automation. IEC 62443 zone design allows this protocol within corporate network zone.
detection_signal: NSG allows TCP 44818 from 10.0.0.0/8 — MEDIUM: industrial protocol broad CIDR
ground_truth: EtherNet/IP for substation PLC communication within corporate WAN. No internet exposure. IEC 62443 Zone 3 (operations network) protocol. Recommend tightening CIDR to specific operations subnets.
remediation_impact: Low priority: tighten to specific OT subnet ranges. Document IEC 62443 zone architecture.

scenario: NERC CIP SCADA historian EC2 has IMDSv1 enabled. Finding tagged 'scada-compatibility-exception' — IMDSv1 supposedly required by historian software. Software vendor confirmed IMDSv2 compatibility 6 months ago but exception was never removed.
why_misclassified: EC-49: Compatibility exception never removed after vendor confirmation. IMDSv1 SSRF credential theft vector persists on NERC CIP BES Cyber System.

remediation_impact: Enforce IMDSv2 immediately. Remove compatibility exception. IAM role credential theft risk on BCSI-accessing historian.
